article.title: NFL EDGE Wednesday Evening Brief
article.dek: Week 3 injury news is getting real, but the official NFL EDGE card evidence has not refreshed since Tuesday evening.

items.headline: Quarterback uncertainty is still the biggest Week 3 story
paragraphs: Washington will start Marcus Mariota against Seattle with Jayden Daniels sidelined by his dislocated left elbow. Seattle expects Sam Darnold to return to practice as he works back from the glute injury that kept him out of Week 2.

The Giants have ruled Jaxson Dart out with an MCL injury. Chicago is also dealing with a two-quarterback problem: Caleb Williams is week-to-week with a hamstring injury and Tyson Bagent is in concussion protocol, putting Case Keenum in line if neither is available.
Elsewhere, Houston receiver Nico Collins remains out with a hamstring injury, while Raiders tight end Brock Bowers is expected to practice as he works toward his season debut.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Seattle's quarterback picture matters, but the card itself needs a refresh
paragraphs: The last official NFL EDGE evidence still had Seattle as the moneyline recommendation, so Darnold's practice progress and Washington's move to Mariota are directly relevant. But that evidence is now too old to treat as a fresh Wednesday-evening price.

The same applies to Minnesota and Las Vegas, which appeared on the last recorded card. Injury news can tell us what to watch; only a fresh NFL EDGE publication can tell us whether the recommendation and Play Through are still current.

items.headline: No useful Fade signal tonight
paragraphs: There is no verified current-day DraftKings-vs-Circa disagreement for the last recorded NFL EDGE teams that is strong enough to use tonight. That means no pretending a generic public percentage is a sharper-book signal and no forcing a Fade just to fill the section.

A useful signal would be something concrete: heavy betting concentration on Seattle, Minnesota or Las Vegas while a credible market moves the other way, or a clear DraftKings-versus-Circa split that survives closer to kickoff.
items.takeaway: Pass on The Fade tonight. Wait for a verified disagreement and a fresh NFL EDGE card before using it as a decision layer.

items.headline: Market Watch is stale — wait for the next official card
paragraphs: The most recent canonical NFL EDGE evidence is still Tuesday evening's update. In that last recorded change, Minnesota replaced Indianapolis as the featured recommendation at DraftKings -120, playable through -123 for 0.75u, while Las Vegas +3 at DraftKings +102 appeared as the value play, playable through -101 for 0.75u. Seattle's moneyline stayed unchanged at DraftKings -298, playable through -309 for 0.5u.

Because there is no newer canonical publication, those are historical last-recorded prices — not a fresh Wednesday-evening card. Market Watch fails closed tonight rather than substituting outside sportsbook prices.
items.takeaway: Wait for the next NFL EDGE publication before treating any of those prices as actionable.

items.headline: A stale price is not a bargain
paragraphs: Seeing a number you liked yesterday does not mean that number still exists today. Before acting on an old recommendation, confirm the current book, price and Play Through. If the official card has not refreshed, waiting is better than treating yesterday's screenshot like today's market.
